title: Assignment 1
text:
Data

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def make_xor(n_points):
    centers = np.array([[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1]])
    labels = np.array([0,1,1,0])
    data = np.array([]).reshape(-1,3)
    for center, label in zip(centers,labels):
        points = np.random.normal(loc=center,scale=0.2,size=(n_points//4,2))
        points_labels = np.hstack((points,label*np.ones(n_points//4).reshape((-1, 1))))
        data = np.vstack((data,points_labels))
    #data = data[np.random.choice(len(data), len(data), replace=False), :]
    return (data[:,[0,1]],data[:,2])

X, y = make_xor(1000)

X_train, y_train = X[:800], y[:800]
X_test, y_test = X[800:], y[800:]
y=y.astype(np.int64)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(X[:,0], X[:,1], s=40, c=y, cmap=plt.cm.Spectral)
plt.show()

text: This is the homepage for Spring 2027 DS6050: ML III: Deep Learning.

title: DS6050: ML III: Deep Learning
text:
Class Description
This is a graduate-level course on machine learning with fundamental concepts for computational data analysis, including pattern recognition, prediction, and visualization. Topics include applied math, machine learning basics, deep neural networks, convolutional networks, sequence modeling, generative learning, and deep reinforcement learning. The course will focus on using open-source libraries such as NumPy and PyTorch. Students are required to have sufficient computational background to complete several substantive programming assignments.
Lecture Time:
    Section 1: 10:00AM – 10:50AM MWF
    Section 2: 11:00AM – 11:50AM MWF
Location: SDS 306

title: DS6050: ML III: Deep Learning
text:
Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of this course, you will be able to:

Create an end-to-end machine learning project at scale using open-source libraries such as NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, and Google Cloud.
Formulate various supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning models, as well as large language models.
Apply practical skill sets on designing, deploying, and analyzing deep network architectures on complex real-world problems.
Articulate concepts, algorithms, and tools to build intelligent systems.
Analyze advanced approaches currently pursued by the machine learning community.

title: DS6050: ML III: Deep Learning

This webpage hosts all needed information for this course. There will also be a canvas page where you will submit your assignments and projects. You must monitor both resources to stay on top of your deadlines.

title: DS6050: ML III: Deep Learning
text:
What’s new this year?
Last year, I collected feedback from the class to see what they wanted added. Their main request was more coding. In response, I have added a new codebase that we will build as a class this semester. I call it minDL, as it is a minimal implementation of deep learning algorithms. You will then have jupyter notebook assignments that rely on your implementations within minDL.

title: minDL: A minimal python codebase for implementing deep learning algorithms
text: Throughout DL6050, you will each be building a codebase for your deep learning methods.

title: minDL: A minimal python codebase for implementing deep learning algorithms
text:
Setup & Tutorial
I’ve implemented the skeleton of this codebase for you here: minDL. Your first task is to set this codebase up on your own, which is your first assignment.
